title: The maximal unramified base locus of a group algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $q:G\to B$ be a group algebraic space locally of finite type. Here a group algebraic space means an algebraic space $G$ with multiplication $G\times_B G\to G$, identity section $B\to G$ and inverse $G\to G$ satisfying the group identities. There exists a largest open subspace $V(G/B)\subseteq B$ such that $G\times_B V(G/B)\to V(G/B)$ is unramified. Every open subspace $W\subseteq B$ for which $G\times_B W\to W$ is unramified is contained in $V(G/B)$. For every morphism of algebraic spaces $h:B'\to B$, the base-changed group $G'=G\times_B B'$ is locally of finite type over $B'$ and $V(G'/B')=B'\times_B V(G/B)$ as open subspaces of $B'$. An open subspace means an open immersion, tested after scheme base change; For a morphism of algebraic spaces, locally of finite type and unramified are tested etale locally on source and target using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], respectively.

proof.text: For any $h:B^\prime\to B$, [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] supplies the algebraic space $G^\prime=G\times_B B^\prime$. On a test scheme $T\to B^\prime$, its sections are the sections of $G$ over $T\to B$; the original multiplication, identity and inverse therefore define its group operations and satisfy the same identities. For every scheme $T\to B$, the same fibre-product statement makes $G\times_B T$ an algebraic space. Thus $q$, viewed as a map of algebraic stacks, is representable by algebraic spaces, as required by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Its arbitrary-base-change clause for locally finite type morphisms gives local finite type of $q^\prime:G^\prime\to B^\prime$. In particular this applies to restriction along every open $W\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tag 0DSJ (1), base-change setup; lemma-base-change-group-space; Tag 03XH (lemma-base-change-finite-type) for local finite type.

proof.text: Let $e:B\to G$ be the identity section. Apply [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change] to $q$ and write $U=U(q)\subseteq G$. Define $V=B\times_{G,e}U$, as a subfunctor of $B$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. It is an open subspace: for every scheme $T\to B$, the pullback is $T\times_G U$, an open subscheme of $T$ by the definition of an open subspace. This is precisely the scheme open-immersion convention [def-weil-open-immersion], and proves openness without an assertion about the image of a morphism.

source.place: Tag 0DSJ (1), proof: take U=e^{-1}(W), with W the unramified source locus from Tag 05W2.

proof.text: For $q_V:G\times_B V\to V$, [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change] gives $U(q_V)=(G\times_B V)\times_G U$. Let $v:V\to B$ and $a:V\to U$ be the projections defining $V=B\times_G U$, so $j a=e v$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow G$. The identity $e_V:V\to G\times_B V$ has composite $e v$ with the projection to $G$. Thus $(e_V,a)$ defines a map $V\to U(q_V)$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], factoring $e_V$ through this open. Hence $q_V$ is unramified at every identity point. Step 1 supplies the group structure and local finite type. Applying [lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-identity-test] to $q_V$ proves that it is unramified on its entire source.

source.place: Tag 0DSJ (1), proof: apply Tag 0DSI to the base change over e^{-1}(W).

proof.text: Let $w:W\hookrightarrow B$ be open with $q_W:G\times_B W\to W$ unramified. Its entire source is an admissible unramified open, so maximality of the source locus gives $U(q_W)=G\times_B W$. By [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change], this is $(G\times_B W)\times_G U$. Thus the projection to $G$ factors through $j:U\hookrightarrow G$. Compose this factorization with the identity of $q_W$ to obtain $u:W\to U$ with $j u=e w$. The fibre-product universal property of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives the unique map $(w,u):W\to B\times_G U=V$ over $B$. Both $W$ and $V$ are subfunctors of $B$, so this is the inclusion $W\subseteq V$. Step 3 proves that $V$ itself works, hence it is the largest such open.

source.place: Tag 0DSJ (1), maximality of U=e^{-1}(W) in its proof.

proof.text: For arbitrary $h:B^\prime\to B$, let $p:G^\prime\to G$ be the projection and $e^\prime:B^\prime\to G^\prime$ the pulled-back identity, so $p e^\prime=e h$. Step 1 gives a locally finite type group over $B^\prime$. By [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change], $U(q^\prime)=G^\prime\times_G U$. Steps 2--4 over $B^\prime$ construct its largest base open as $B^\prime\times_{G^\prime,e^\prime}(G^\prime\times_G U)$. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow G$. On any scheme $T$, an element of this last fibre product is a pair $b^\prime:T\to B^\prime$, $u:T\to U$ with $e h b^\prime=j u$: the intervening $G^\prime$ coordinate is forced to equal $e^\prime b^\prime$. The same pair determines $(b^\prime,(h b^\prime,u))$ in $B^\prime\times_B(B\times_G U)=B^\prime\times_B V$, and forgetting the forced coordinate is its inverse. These maps commute with every pullback of $T$ and preserve $b^\prime$. The sheaf fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] therefore identifies the two open subfunctors over $B^\prime$. This proves $V(G^\prime/B^\prime)=B^\prime\times_B V(G/B)$ for every $h$, including nonreduced base changes.

lean.statement: theorem groupSpace_unramified_base_locus {S : Scheme.{u}} (B G : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : G ⟶ B) [@GrpObj (Over B.obj) _ (Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory B.obj) (Over.mk q.hom)] (hlft : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) q) : ∃ (V : AlgebraicSpace S) (v : V ⟶ B), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) v.hom.hom ∧ MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) (enlargedFibreProductFst v q) ∧ (∀ (W : AlgebraicSpace S) (w : W ⟶ B), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) w.hom.hom → MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) (enlargedFibreProductFst w q) → ∃ i : W ⟶ V, i ≫ v = w) ∧ (∀ (B' : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : B' ⟶ B), MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) (enlargedFibreProductFst h q) ∧ MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) (enlargedFibreProductFst (enlargedFibreProductFst h v) (enlargedFibreProductFst h q)) ∧ (∀ (W : AlgebraicSpace S) (w : W ⟶ B'), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) w.hom.hom → (MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) (enlargedFibreProductFst w (enlargedFibreProductFst h q)) ↔ ∃ i : W ⟶ enlargedFibreProduct h v, i ≫ enlargedFibreProductFst h v = w)))
lean.note: The arbitrary-base-change clause characterizes the pulled-back open by admissibility and the factorization iff for all open subspaces, so it states equality of the largest opens without choosing their representatives. GrpObj uses the explicit standard pullback cartesian structure on Over B.obj. Two landed statement dependencies name the existing chart test and bundled sheaf fibre products.
